units.title: Algebraic expressions and equations
units.why: Algebra models unknown quantities and supports every later function topic.
principles: perform the same operation on both sides
misconceptions: changing a sign without applying it to every term
practice: Explain why division by zero is invalid.

videoPackage.title: Algebra foundations
videoPackage.transcript: We model an equation as a balance, simplify one legal step at a time, and substitute the answer to check it.

units.title: Number patterns
units.why: Patterns prepare learners for sequences, functions and modelling change.
principles: constant first differences indicate an arithmetic pattern
a rule must work for every listed term
practice: Explain why two terms do not prove a rule.
solutions: many rules can fit two points

videoPackage.title: Reading number patterns
videoPackage.transcript: We compare neighbouring terms, identify the operation, and verify the rule against more than one term.

units.title: Linear and quadratic functions
units.why: Functions describe dependable input-output relationships in science and finance.
principles: a function assigns one output to each allowed input
the gradient measures change in y per unit x
misconceptions: confusing an input with an output
practice: Make a value table for y=x+2 at x=0,1,2.
State the range restriction for a square root.
Explain why a vertical line is not a function.
solutions: one input would have multiple outputs

videoPackage.title: Functions as machines
videoPackage.transcript: A function maps an allowed input to exactly one output; tables and graphs make the rule visible.

units.title: Euclidean geometry and measurement
units.why: Geometry gives a language for space, proof and measurement.
principles: angles on a straight line sum to 180°
similar figures have proportional corresponding sides
examples: a triangle with angles 50° and 60° has third angle 70°
practice: Find circumference using π=3.14 for r=5.

videoPackage.title: Proof through measurement
videoPackage.transcript: We label known angles and lengths, apply one theorem at a time, and attach units to every measurement.

units.title: Trigonometric ratios
units.why: Trigonometry connects angles and distances in surveying, construction and physics.
misconceptions: using the wrong side relative to the chosen angle
practice: Find adjacent when cosθ=.8 and hypotenuse=15.
Why must calculator mode be checked?
Give one real use of trigonometry.
quizQuestions: What is an angle of elevation?

videoPackage.title: Choosing a trig ratio
videoPackage.transcript: We name the sides from the chosen angle, choose the ratio containing the known and unknown sides, and check units.
